models.score_source: ESTIMATE (Artificial Analysis has published v5.0.1 component scores but no index yet; fetched 2026-11-06): HLE 8.9, GPQA-Diamond 70.2, SciCode 26.3, AA-LCR 59.3, Terminal-Bench 2.1 8.6, tau2-Banking 20.8, GDPval 714.9, HLE-Diamond 3.8, CritPT v2 Hard 0.3, AutomationBench 1.8. A kNN fit over the 44 AA-scored models sharing those components gives 5.9, rounded down to 5.8 for the weak Terminal-Bench row. The vendor card (OpenBMB, 2026-09-07) calls it 2B-class SOTA. Treat as UNVERIFIED; plausible range 4.8-6.8.
models.notes: Released 2026-09-07. 2,516,756,480 total / 1,981,982,720 non-embedding parameters, 42 layers, 131,072-token context, built for on-device assistants and coding/tool workflows. Only 2 KV heads keep the cache small (42 KiB/token at f16), so Q4_K_M plus 64K context with q4_0 KV still fits a 4 GB budget (2.77 GiB total). Emits XML-style tool calls; llama.cpp needs --jinja, SGLang has a native minicpm5 parser. Q4_K_M is the official file; IQ4_XS and Q5_K_M are bartowski files in the same quant list.

models.name: Qwen3 Coder Next
models.score_source: ESTIMATE: no official AA v5 index. Predicted from AA's published v5 components (AutomationBench 1%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 0%, GDP.pdf 2.6%, AA-Briefcase 404 Elo) via linear fit on 107 models with an official v5 index (RMSE 3.0 pts) -> 5.3. The low AA-Briefcase score drags the general index down; for coding agents the model is stronger than that. Legacy-component fit gives 6.9.
models.notes: Released 2026-02-03. Coding-agent specialist: 512 experts, top-10, 3B active, hybrid Gated DeltaNet with 12 full-attention layers out of 48. Non-thinking only (no  thinking blocks). 256k native context. At Q5_K_M it is 56.7GB, so it is the model to run when the 64GB box is a coding box.

models.name: Granite 4.2 8B
models.score_source: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (artificialanalysis.ai leaderboard JSON, fetched 2026-11-02)
models.notes: Released 2026-08-25. Already in the catalog; kept here because it is the best-scoring model at this tier with an official AA v5 number. Dense GQA transformer (not the 4.0 hybrid Mamba), 128K native, reasoning-augmented tool calling. Its KV cache is the expensive part: 40 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 = 160KiB/token at f16, so 8K context needs ~1.2GiB; use q8_0 KV (0.61GiB) and Q5_0 to stay under 7GiB. Enterprise/Apache alternative to Qwen/Ornith.

models.name: Ministral 3 8B Reasoning
models.score_source: ESTIMATE: vendor reasoning-card numbers of 2025-12-02 (AIME25 78.7, GPQA Diamond 66.8, LiveCodeBench 61.6) are near Qwen3.5 9B (catalog 5.0); AA's 2026-11-06 run of the same family is lower (GPQA 47.1, HLE 4.3, LCB 30.3) because it does not enable the thinking mode, so the card numbers are used for the thinking-mode score. Set 5.0, midpoint of the two. Composite is UNVERIFIED.
models.notes: Released 2025-12-02 (AA model page). 8.4B language model plus a 0.4B vision encoder, 34 layers, 8 KV heads x 128, 256K context, Apache-2.0. The reasoning post-trained variant; keep reasoning traces in context and use the vendor system prompt. Native function calling and JSON output. Vision needs the 858 MB F16 mmproj, which EZLM does not load today. UD-Q3_K_XL at 16K with q4_0 KV is ~5.1 GiB; IQ4_XS at 8K is ~5.1 GiB.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.score_source: ESTIMATE: v5-equivalent predicted from AA's own published v5 component scores (AutomationBench, Terminal-Bench 4.0, HLE-Diamond, GDP.pdf, AA-Briefcase) via linear fit on 90 models with official v5 index (RMSE 1.7 pts); model not yet given an official v5 index: 9B predicted 6.3 (legacy fit 2.3) -> 5 (catalog value, unchanged)
models.notes: Released 2026-02/03. Still the current small Qwen (no Qwen3.6/3.8 at this size) and now clearly outclassed by Ornith-1.5-9B, which uses the same architecture: Ornith card puts Qwen3.5-9B at Terminal-Bench 2.1 21.3 vs 46.2, SWE-bench Verified 53.2 vs 70.6. Kept for its 32KiB/token KV cache (8x cheaper than Granite 4.2 8B at long context), native 262K context, vision mmproj and mature llama.cpp support. Catalog quants trimmed to those that fit 8GB; Q6_K (6.95GiB) is too tight once KV and buffers are counted.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B
models.score_source: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (artificialanalysis.ai, fetched 2026-11-06): 4.65
models.notes: Released 2026-04-29. Dense 128B, unified instruct/reasoning/coding with per-request reasoning effort, multimodal input, 256k context. Lowest score in this tier but the only dense 128B that fits, and dense decode is steadier than MoE on unified memory. The KV cache is the constraint (352KiB/token): IQ2_M (44.1GB) leaves room for a 32k context, Q3_K_S (54.4GB) only about 16k. GGUFs built before the 2026-07 config fix have degraded long-context behaviour, so pin to a recent file. Vision adds mmproj-F16.gguf (5.4GB), which pushes Q3_K_S over 64GB even at 16k; pair vision with IQ2_M.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B
models.score_source: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models, fetched 2026-11-06), official index. The catalog's 8.0 estimate (2026-11-02, legacy-component fit) is superseded by this published number.
models.notes: Released 2026-02. 60 layers: 50 sliding (16 KV x 256, window 1024) + 10 global (4 KV x 512). The SWA cache is ~2.3 GB at 8K and does not grow with context, so the 8.53 GB IQ2_XXS fits a 12 GB card only in split mode at 16K (~8 tok/s), and not a 10 GB unified budget. AA components: GPQA 85.7%, TB2.1 43.4%, tau2 59.9%, IFBench 75.6%. Use it when image quality matters more than speed; Gemma 4 12B is the fast 6-bit alternative.

models.name: EXAONE 4.5 33B
models.score_source: ESTIMATE: legacy fit (HLE 12.9%, AA-LCR 54.7%, GDPval-AA 474.5, CritPt 0.3%) on 87 models with an official v5 index (RMSE 4.9) -> 4.2. AA has no v5 components for it yet (tau2 78.1%, GPQA 79.4%, TB-hard 20.5% are v4-era). Fetched 2026-11-06.
models.notes: Released 2026-04-04. 33B dense model plus a 1.2B vision encoder (34.35B counted), 262K context, 3:1 sliding-window (4096) to full attention over 65 blocks, one of which is an MTP layer. Multilingual (en, ko, es, de, ja, vi) with strong document understanding. AA components fetched 2026-11-06: tau2 78.1%, GPQA 79.4%, HLE 12.9%, AA-LCR 54.7%, IFBench 58.0%, TB-hard 20.5%. License is EXAONE 1.2-NC: research and non-commercial use only, which blocks a paid deployment. Tool calling is in the chat template; vision needs the separate mmproj file.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B
models.score_source: ESTIMATE: v5-equivalent predicted from AA's legacy v4-era components (HLE, AA-LCR, GDPval-AA, CritPt) via linear fit on 83 models with official v5 index (RMSE 4.9 pts), cross-checked against partial v5 components: legacy fit 3.3 (catalog value, unchanged)
models.notes: Released 2026-05-23 ('unified' any-to-any: text, image, audio in; text out). 40 sliding-window layers (8 KV x 256, window 1024) plus 8 global layers (1 KV x 512). The sliding-window cache is a fixed ~0.94GiB at 8K context and does not grow, so the KV cost is dominated by it, not by context length. That is why only Q3-class quants fit 8GB: IQ4_XS (5.94GiB) plus cache and buffers is ~7.4GiB, too much for a 7.0GiB unified budget. Best reason to pick it is the any-to-any input and Google tooling; it is the weakest general model of the six.

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B
models.score_source: ESTIMATE (no AA v5): NVIDIA model card 2026-10-05 benchmarks against Gemma-4-E4B-it (catalog 2.0) and Qwen3.5-4B (catalog 2.0). Bolt wins MultiChallenge 53.1 vs 42.1/51.8, RoleBench 67.1 vs 50.0/53.7, BFCL-v3 68.5 vs 66.4/71.0, ToolSandbox 68.8 vs 65.4/69.5, Tau2-Bench 55.1 vs 38.5/75.1, IFBench 63.8 vs 42.8/58.9, LongMemEval 72.1 vs 71.0/66.9; loses Tau2 to Qwen3.5-4B. -> 3.5, vendor-reported.
models.notes: Released 2026-10-05. NVIDIA post-train of Gemma-4-E4B (gemma4 arch, 8.0B total / 4B effective via per-layer embeddings), built for low-TTFT voice and device assistants. 42 blocks, 18 trailing layers share a KV cache, so only 4 global + 20 sliding-window caches are allocated: 16KiB/token global plus a fixed ~0.1GiB window cache. That makes it the long-context pick of this tier: UD-Q5_K_XL (5.43GiB) plus a 64K cache and buffers is ~6.9GiB, so it runs the full 64K at Q5 on an 8GB machine. Also the cheapest at high context. Vendor states 64K input though the GGUF advertises 131072. DFlash drafter (0.37GiB) is available for speculative decoding. Weaker at hard reasoning and code than the three 9B-class models.

models.name: LFM2.5 8B A1B
models.license: LFM Open License v1.0 (free below a revenue threshold; UNVERIFIED amount)
models.score_source: ESTIMATE: AA per-benchmark run of 2026-11-06 (GPQA Diamond 51.3, HLE 6.9, IFBench 55.6, tau2 16.1) is below Gemma 4 12B (catalog 3.5) and above Qwen3.5 4B (2.0); set 3.0. AA has no v5 Intelligence Index for it. Composite is UNVERIFIED.
models.notes: Released 2026-05-28 (AA model page). Hybrid MoE: 8.3B total, 1.5B active (32 experts, 4 used), 24 blocks of which 18 are double-gated convolutions and only 6 are GQA attention, so the KV cache is small. 128K context, 128K vocab, 10 languages. Q4_0 at 32K with q4_0 KV is ~5.2 GiB (64K ~5.5), Q4_K_M at 32K is ~5.5 GiB. Edge/CPU friendly and fast; weaker knowledge and heavy coding than the K2 models. LFM Open License v1.0.

models.name: Kimi Linear 48B A3B Instruct
models.score_source: ESTIMATE (no v5 index): AA v4-era components GPQA 41.2%, HLE 2.5%, AA-LCR 28.0%, LiveCodeBench 37.8%, AIME-2025 36.3% imply a low v5 index (about 2); the legacy fit needs GDPval and CritPt, which AA did not publish for this model. Fetched 2026-11-06. Treat as a long-context specialist, not a general pick.
models.notes: Released 2025-10-30. Kimi Delta Attention (linear attention) with 7 full-attention layers out of 27; 48B total, 3B active, 256 experts top-8. 1M context and a very small cache: 1.0GB at 64K, 4.1GB at 256K, 16.5GB at 1M f16 (MLA, one KV head). MIT. AA components fetched 2026-11-06: GPQA 41.2%, HLE 2.5%, AA-LCR 28.0%, LiveCodeBench 37.8%, AIME-2025 36.3%. Dated against 2026 models; kept only because it is the cheapest way to get a real 1M-token window at this memory tier. Tool calling is in the chat template.
